alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes And (rule 14).

The wayyiqtol of hayah in the periphrastic hayu + participle: the ASV collapses the clause to a simple past and writes no auxiliary or copula for it. Corrected from a rule 30 fusion with the participle. Rule 30's contiguity condition is unmet, the subject ha-kerubim standing between the two verbs exactly as a subject standing between a verb and its preposition defeats that condition there; and the one-English-rendering condition is unmet too, since spread out is wholly the participle's own lexeme plus its phrasal particle under rule 44, so no part of it is unowned. Rule 35's far side does not rescue it, because that reaches a single English word carrying every morpheme's sense. The competing reading fuses the two into spread out headed on the participle; the deciding evidence is that the verse's other hayu, in toward the mercy seat were the faces, is written out as were while this one is not.
Participle rendered by the phrasal verb spread out; the particle stays with the verb and the head is the lexical verb (rule 44).

The Hebrew participial construct writes kenaphayim bare, with no pronominal suffix and no article; a supplied possessive answers to no morpheme (rules 18, 30). Contrast bekanpehem later in the verse, which does write a suffix and takes its own their.
Directive he fused with its host into the single English high (rule 32).
The ASV recasts ha-kapporeth as a bare direct object of covering, leaving the preposition nothing to say (rule 40).
One substantive rendered mercy seat, headed on the lexeme-bearing mercy (rule 31).
Construct noun keeps its own word.
Waw rendered by the connective with, which rule 14 keeps on the conjunction.
Noun and its suffix fused into the single English another (rule 30); the suffix's sense is inside that word, so it is not an unrendered occurrence (rule 22).
Finite verb rendered were; unlike the verse's first hayu, this one has an English word of its own.
Construct noun takes a supplied the, the rectum's own article standing before its own word (rule 29).
Article takes the the standing before its own word (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the relational of (rule 19), headed on the noun.

review_notes: Corrected one unit: the accepted alignment fused the wayyiqtol hayu with the participle poresei into spread out. Rule 30's contiguity condition fails, the subject standing between them, and the participle owns the whole English rendering including its phrasal particle under rule 44, so nothing is left unowned for a fusion to carry. The finite verb is now unrepresented and the participle keeps spread out.
The their of their wings remains added: kenaphayim is written bare, with neither suffix nor article, so no morpheme licenses a possessive (rules 18, 30).
The al before ha-kapporeth remains unrepresented, the ASV promoting the phrase to a direct object of covering (rule 40).
All 30 source and 32 target ids are partitioned exactly once after the correction.
